sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared test data setup
sections.what: Creates two users, a shared crew, a solo crew, a report, a block, a scored match and an analytics event for the tests to use.
sections.why: Likely reason: export and deletion are only meaningful with realistic linked data.
sections.watch_out: Later tests rely on this data existing, so running one test alone can give different counts.

sections.name: account: export my data
sections.title: Exporting user data
sections.what: Checks that the export contains the format name, the user details, crews, teams, scoring and events, and no password text.
sections.why: Likely reason: users have a right to their data, and secrets must not be included.
sections.watch_out: The password check is a text search that only catches the hash patterns it lists.

sections.name: account: delete my account
sections.title: Deleting an account and append-only scoring
sections.what: Checks deletion removes the user and their linked rows, passes a shared crew to the friend, removes solo crews, and that scoring events cannot be deleted outside an erasure.
sections.why: Likely reason: deletion must be complete, while the scoring record stays protected.
sections.watch_out: Changing the rule that protects scoring events affects this test directly.

summary: Unit tests for the account features: exporting a user's data without secrets, and deleting an account while keeping shared crews and the scoring record protected.
purpose: Protects the privacy rights to export and erase data, and keeps the scoring history append-only.
why: Likely reason: users must be able to get their data and remove it, and the scoring record must stay trustworthy.
how: Before the tests, it resets the database and creates a user who will leave, a friend, a shared crew, a solo crew, a report, a block, a finished-scoring match, and an analytics event. The export test checks the format name, user details, crew, team, scoring and event counts, and that no password text appears. The deletion test removes the user, checks their rows are gone, hands the shared crew to the friend, and removes the solo crew. The last test confirms scoring events cannot be deleted outside an erasure.
inputs: Seeded test data created in the test database.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The tests share one data set and depend on running in order, so changing one test can change the counts in another. The append-only test uses a raw delete command.
debug: If the deletion test fails, check the counts for each table it lists. If the append-only test fails, look for the rule that rejects deletes and its error text.
